cells.tense: Something you have tended is finished, and you are still holding it, so your hands are full today.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Let a finished thing be finished in your own mind, and keep your hands on the part that's still alive.
cells.core:
You learn what you care for by handling it — sowing, waiting, watching what answers your attention and what doesn't. That isn't theorizing. It's apprenticeship, and the material is patient about being learned. The same patience that lets a thing come up in its own time is what keeps the asking honest. When the timing is off, your hands know it before you can name it.

Some slowness you carry isn't doubt. It's the recognition that a thing is done and pulling for your attention anyway. So let a finished one be finished. Keep tending the rest. You'll know the difference by what you stop explaining. Release doesn't have to wait for a feeling of readiness — it can just be what the work asks for when the work is finished.
cells.sheetLine: You tend what's growing and can let the finished part go.
cells.verb: tending what is growing, learning its pace from it
cells.place: the place where what is still forming is cared for

cells.tense: The seed is still in the ground, but you're pacing the field asking whether the harvest will be worth it.
cells.act: envision it freshly and feel toward it
cells.ask: Picture one way the growing thing could go well and let yourself want that version, then make one move today that serves it.
cells.core:
Care that runs ahead stops being care. You tend what's growing, and when you're carrying the whole outcome at once, the hand gets a grip to it — more water, more checking, a pull at the stem to see if the root took. The growing thing feels it. What it needs is a hand that isn't braced.

The way through isn't less feeling. It's the same care turned one step further. Picture one way this could go well, then want that version rather than the whole future. Once you've seen it, make one move today that only makes sense if that picture holds. You're not deciding what will happen. You're giving the next step a direction to serve.
cells.sheetLine: You're out past the growing thing, living in its harvest. Come back.
cells.verb: tending what is growing, learning its pace from it
cells.place: the place where what is still forming is cared for

cells.tense: You used to have your hands in the soil, and lately you stand at the edge of it.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin a small piece of something this week and carry it only as far as the beginning, with nothing owed past that.
cells.core:
Something you once did with attention has gone quiet in your hands. What you were tending is still there, and the care hasn't come. There's a distance between you and what's growing, and it's the kind that widens if nothing is put to work. The instinct is to push yourself back in — more effort, more feeling — and that isn't what's missing.

What's missing is a beginning with no future attached. Take a row of herbs, a page, a repair — whatever's small — and begin it for the beginning alone. You don't need to know how it ends. You need your own hand on something again, doing a thing it knows how to do, with nothing required of it past that. The care comes back through the hand, not through wishing for it.
cells.sheetLine: Begin something small for the pleasure of beginning it.
cells.verb: tending what is growing, learning its pace from it
cells.place: the place where what is still forming is cared for

cells.tense: You are the one keeping this growing, and you would say you are just passing through.
cells.act: govern by knowing what to surrender
cells.ask: Notice a thing you keep alive, name to yourself that you keep it alive, then let part of it carry forward without your hands.
cells.core:
The care is happening. Plants get watered, plans get made, people get looked after — and when you're asked about it, you were somewhere else. That story has held a while. The evidence against it is not in your feelings; it's in what grew.

Nothing here needs to be announced to anyone. Take a thing you're keeping alive and say, without decoration, that you are keeping it alive. Then notice what it could carry without you. That second part is where the strength shows: you don't have to name yourself as the grower for anyone — only long enough to see what can stand when your hands come off it. That's the whole work of a finished hand.
cells.sheetLine: Say quietly that you are the one keeping it alive.
cells.verb: tending what is growing, learning its pace from it
cells.place: the place where what is still forming is cared for

attempts.check: The mechanism claim in Too Little — that the person has stepped back from tending — is read from the draw, not from any account of their life; a reader could fairly say they are still tending plenty and just tired. The ask survives a wrong read because doing one thing fully and well, then stopping, is useful whether or not the starvation is real. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person: any line explaining that the seed was once taken from them — cut, because the record does not support a history. Too Much does not announce itself as crossing into daydream; it shows as pushing the growing thing past its own timing.

The ask survives a wrong read because tending something without a purpose attached is useful whether or not anything was lost. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any line explaining why the quiet came — cut, because the record supports no history. attempts.check: The Too Little cell says attention has gone quiet in the person's hands; that is read from the draw, not from any account of their life, and a reader could fairly say they still tend plenty and are simply worn thin. The ask stands even if the read is wrong, because beginning a thing with no future attached is worth doing either way. The line that flatters the writer is any explanation of why the quiet came — cut, since the record carries no history. Too Much shows as a hand braced over a seed that hasn't come up. The Unacknowledged ask is a noticing rather than a doing, which is what that medicine is: authorship can't be claimed by an act the person can't see they already perform. This rewrite varies the ask shapes — one release, one picture plus move, one start, one noticing plus handoff — and leaves three of the four without a clock.
